author: Fang, Cathy Mengying and Liu, Auren R. and Danry, Valdemar and Lee, Eunhae and Chan, Samantha W. T. and Pataranutaporn, Pat and Maes, Pattie and Phang, Jason and Lampe, Michael and Ahmad, Lama and Agarwal, Sandhini
title: How AI and Human Behaviors Shape Psychosocial Effects of Extended Chatbot Use: A Longitudinal Randomized Controlled Study
design: Four-week randomized comparison of chatbot modes and topics; n=981
finding: Revised abstract reports no significant assigned-condition effects; heavier voluntary use is associated with worse outcomes.
limit: Usage intensity was not randomized; socialization is not a count of requests to friends.

author: Guingrich, Rose E. and Graziano, Michael S. A.
title: A Longitudinal Randomized Control Study of Companion Chatbot Use: Anthropomorphism and Its Mediating Role on Social Impacts
design: 21-day randomized chatbot versus word-game comparison; n=183
outcome: Social health, loneliness, perceived relationship impacts
finding: No overall significant condition differences; perceived impacts vary with anthropomorphism.
limit: Perceived impact is not observed outreach; magnitude and direction of impact differ.
locator: Methods: Social Impact; Results; Appendix A

author: Chandra, Mohit and Hernandez, Javier and Ramos, Gonzalo and Ershadi, Mahsa and Bhattacharjee, Ananya and Amores, Judith and Okoli, Ebele and Paradiso, Ann and Warreth, Shahed and Suh, Jina
title: Longitudinal Study on Social and Emotional Use of AI Conversational Agent
design: Five-week exploratory active-use versus usual-use groups; n=149
outcome: Attachment, perceived empathy, comfort seeking AI support
finding: Active users reported increased attachment and greater comfort seeking support from AI.
limit: AI comfort does not establish reduced human outreach; recruitment and retention limit inference.

author: De Freitas, Julian and O{\u{g}}uz-U{\u{g}}uralp, Zeliha and U{\u{g}}uralp, Ahmet Kaan and Puntoni, Stefano
title: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
design: Multi-study paper: reviews, experiments, one-week longitudinal study
finding: Chatbot interactions can reduce momentary loneliness; this does not establish lasting relief between interactions.
limit: Loneliness relief and substitution of human requests are distinct outcomes.
locator: Studies 2–5; General Discussion, author PDF p.19

author: Meng, Jingbo and Dai, Yue Nancy
title: Emotional Support from AI Chatbots: Should a Supportive Partner Self-Disclose or Not?
access: Institutional abstract and metadata; PDF retrieval failed
design: Online experiment varying source, support, and self-disclosure
outcome: Stress and worry reduction; perceived supportiveness
finding: Support effects depend on the partner and reciprocal self-disclosure.
limit: Immediate distress relief does not measure later contact with friends.
locator: Institutional abstract; methods not independently inspected

author: Meng, Jingbo and Zhang, Renwen and Qin, Jiaqi and Lee, Yu-Jen and Lee, Yi-Chieh
title: AI-mediated social support: the prospect of human--AI collaboration
design: Study of human/AI support-message production and evaluation
finding: Patterns of human–AI collaboration are associated with different message features and evaluations.
limit: Support provision is not the same as a seeker contacting an existing friend.
role: Bridging context, not a bridging estimate

author: Young, Jordyn and Jawara, Laala M. and Nguyen, Diep N. and Daly, Brian and Huh-Yoo, Jina and Razi, Afsaneh
title: The Role of AI in Peer Support for Young People: A Study of Preferences for Human- and AI-Generated Responses
status: arXiv version reviewed; venue status not independently verified
design: Survey evaluating blinded support responses; n=622
outcome: Response preferences, helpfulness, willingness to send
finding: Evaluations differ by response source and topic; AI responses were preferred for several topics.
limit: Rating supplied messages does not show subsequent human support-seeking.

author: Skjuve, Marita and F{\o}lstad, Asbj{\o}rn and Fostervold, Knut Inge and Brandtz{\ae}g, Petter Bae
title: My Chatbot Companion -- a Study of Human-Chatbot Relationships
access: Institutional abstract and metadata; full-text redirect unavailable
design: Interviews with 18 people who developed Replika friendships
outcome: Relationship development and perceived social consequences
finding: Participants described valued chatbot relationships and mixed wider social effects.
limit: Selected users and retrospective accounts do not identify a population causal effect.

author: Ueda, Michiko and Birnbaum, Michael L. and Liu, Yanhong and Yu, Qingyi and Tian, Xihe and Mirer, Anna and Ramanathan, Seethalakshmi and Sinyor, Mark
title: Help-Seeking in the Age of AI: Cross-Sectional Survey of the Use and Perceptions of AI-Based Mental Health Support Among US Adults
design: Cross-sectional survey of US adults; n=1805
outcome: Use and attitudes toward AI and professional support
finding: AI users held more favorable attitudes to AI support; attitudes toward human counselors did not vary by AI-use status.
limit: Professional help is outside the primary outcome; attitudes and associations are not behavioral effects.
role: Boundary case; excluded from informal-support synthesis
